Data science

Cardiovascular Data Modelling .

How much do blood pressure, age, and cholesterol tell us about cardiovascular disease in this dataset?

View Demo

Project context

Data Modelling · Team of three

  • Python
  • scikit-learn
  • Streamlit

Research question

Our team investigated two questions. Which measurements help a model distinguish patients with and without cardiovascular disease, and how closely can a regression model estimate systolic blood pressure?

My contribution

I compared logistic regression, gradient boosting, Gaussian naive Bayes, and a neural network. I evaluated the classifiers, measured how accuracy changed when groups of features were removed, and helped prepare the Streamlit application.

Methods and findings

After removing duplicates and filtering implausible measurements, we retained 68,475 of 70,000 records. With a stratified 80/20 train–test split, gradient boosting achieved 73.76% test accuracy and an F1 score of 0.7205. Using just systolic blood pressure, age, and cholesterol yielded 73.18% accuracy. Removing all blood pressure features lowered it to 64.89%.

Team deliverable

Our Streamlit prototype displays predictions, evaluation metrics, and feature importance. For the separate regression task, the team’s model estimated systolic blood pressure with a mean absolute error of 7.20 mmHg on the test data. These results describe performance on this academic dataset.
